terms.comment: From diurna, the daily record (ācta diurna). Lewis & Short has the word once, late, for a keeper of a day-book (Cod. Theod. 8.4.8). A woman is diurnāria (Traupman). Traupman gives the same word for a reporter.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 167, 335, checked against the searchable text of the book.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. journalist.
